text.p: Morgan Stanley & Co. International have upgraded the shares of electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG to outperform from neutral and raised its 1998 earnings estimate.
Morgan Stanley said in a research note that it had a price target of 1,025 Swedish crowns and 2,050 Swiss francs for the shares of the Swedish and Swiss parents of ABB.
The shares of ABB AG, the Swiss company that owns half of ABB, were up three francs at 1,727 at Friday midday and the shares of ABB AB, the Swedish part-owner, were 12 crowns lower at 858 crowns.
Based on Morgan Stanley's estimate, the stocks are trading at a 1998 price/earnings (P/E) ratio of around 13.5, a clear discount to the sector's 17.
"We consider this discount to be unjustified, given the quality of the group and its strong position in South-East Asia and Europe," Morgan Stanley's analysts wrote.
A P/E target of 16 should not be too demanding, implying a share price upside of 19 to 20 percent, Morgan Stanley wrote.
Shares in ABB fell after announcing lower-than-expected 1996 results in late February and a less-than-enthusiastic forecast for the current year due to weak capital goods spending.
Shortly after the results, many analysts reduced their forecasts and downgraded the shares.
Morgan Stanley also cut its 1997 forecast, but raised the 1998 forecast and created a 1999 forecast.
Morgan Stanley estimates that earnings per share (EPS) of Swiss ABB will rise to 106.17 francs in 1997 from 1996's 85.39 and then rise to 126.55 in 1998 and 157.64 in 1999.
EPS for Swedish ABB is estimated to rise to 53.08 crowns in 1997 from 1996's 44.20 and then rise too 63.60 in 1998 and 79.48 in 1999.

The rise in 1997 EPS results is helped by currency factors. The 1997 net income of the ABB group, which reports in U.S. dollars, is forecast to rise seven percent to $1,320 million from 1996's $1,233 million.
"We believe that 1998 and 1999 earnings will look good, and we are forecasting net income growth of 20 and 25 percent, respectively," Morgan Stanley wrote.
But in 1998, ABB and Morgan Stanley expect profits to accelerate on an improving capital goods cycle and restructuring benefits at power generation and the transport business.

"We recognise that the shares may mark time until the expected pick-up in 1998 earnings becomes more visible and confidence is restored in company guidance, but, given the low valuation, we think the shares could move sharply once sentiment turns," Morgan Stanley said.
